sections.h2: Ways to sell a Maryville house
sections.html:
Three routes lead out of a Maryville house: list with an agent, sell it yourself, or take a cash offer for the place as it stands. Which one wins depends on what the roof and kitchen need, how soon you have to be gone and how many open houses you can stand.

Maryville has 32,442 residents as of July 2025, up just 1.7% since 2020. Owners occupy 67.5% of homes, and the 2020-2024 median home value is $358,100. That is a citywide midpoint, so lean on comparable sales near you for a real price.

  • Agent: best for a tidy house and a seller with time to wait for the top bidder.
  • Selling alone: reasonable if you know your way around a purchase contract and closing statement.
  • Cash: often easier with deferred repairs, a tenant in place or an inherited property.

A cash purchase drops showings, the lender's appraisal and the repair list that follows an inspection. A clean title, a recorded deed and settled tax bills still have to happen. Each is covered below.

Two governments tax a Maryville home, the city and Blount County. For 2026 the county charges $1.29 per $100 of assessed value, after three years at $1.59. The city's general fund rate is $1.36 per $100. Houses are assessed at 25% of appraised value.

Blount County tax calendar

Whoever owned the home on January 1 is the name on the roll. At closing, the year's bill is split by days of ownership and the buyer takes over from there. Phone the Trustee at 865-273-5900 or City of Maryville financial services at 865-273-3456 and request payoff figures before you pick a closing date.

A delinquent bill will not block a sale. The title company deducts what is owed from your proceeds, so it needs a current payoff letter from the Trustee and the city.

  • Request written figures dated close to the closing day.
  • Interest at 1.5% a month starts once the end-of-February window closes, so a late payoff grows.
  • If a tax relief or greenbelt status applies to the property, ask what happens to it when the deed changes hands.

Maryville Codes Enforcement works from 416 West Broadway and answers at 865-273-3500. It runs the building and property maintenance rules. Effective January 1, 2026, the council moved to the 2024 International Building, Residential, Mechanical, Energy Conservation, Plumbing and Fire codes plus a 2024 Property Maintenance Code. The 2017 National Electrical Code remains in force.

A buyer's contractor may ask which code edition covered any recent permitted job, so the codes office can answer that for you. State law has also stiffened penalties for construction and maintenance violations. Did you remodel without pulling a permit? Talk with the office before listing, not after an inspector spots it.

Maryville issues short-term rental unit permits. Each application needs a plan and a safety affidavit, and the planning office treats the use as a zoning topic, so verify that your street falls in an allowed district.

  • Applicants sketch the lot and a floor plan marking bedrooms, beds, off-street parking and life safety gear.
  • The owner signs an affidavit covering UL 217 smoke alarms in and near each sleeping room and on every story, a carbon monoxide detector within 15 feet of bedrooms and a working fire extinguisher.
  • Inspectors may check the equipment before the permit issues and again later on reasonable notice.

Selling a house that has hosted guests? Tell the buyer which permit it holds, and call 865-273-3500 to ask whether that permit can pass to a new owner.

sections.h2: Deed recording at the Register of Deeds
sections.html:
Blount County's Register of Deeds sits at 349 Court Street and takes calls at 865-273-5880. A one- or two-page deed costs $12 to record, each extra page is $5, and there is a $1 clerk fee. Tennessee's transfer tax is 37 cents per $100 on top.

Every deed must show the district, map and parcel numbers and name the responsible taxpayer with a mailing address. Trust deeds and mortgages also need the maximum principal indebtedness statement used for recording tax. Enclose a stamped return envelope and the original comes back to you.

One oddity: the city platted more than 250 alleys long ago and is closing the unneeded ones. When an alley closes, ownership usually splits 50/50 between neighbors on either side, and the city drafts and records the quitclaim deeds for free. If your lot borders a platted alley, ask planning whether it was abandoned.

sections.h2: From offer to closing with a cash buyer
sections.html:
1. You describe the property and hand over the documents listed below. The buyer looks it over and names a price.
  2. Once you agree, a title company opens a file, searches ownership history and requests payoffs from the Trustee and the city.
  3. Mortgage balances, liens and back taxes come out of your proceeds.
  4. You sign the deed at closing, and it goes to the Register of Deeds at 349 Court Street.
  5. The current year's tax is divided by days owned.

No lender means no underwriting queue, so the closing date can follow your moving plans.

A conventional buyer in Maryville usually needs a lender, and the lender wants an appraisal, an inspection and sometimes repairs completed before funding. Each of those can derail a closing weeks after you accepted an offer. A cash buyer removes the lender from the picture, so the offer is not contingent on the bank's view of the house.

That matters most with an older roof, outdated wiring or a kitchen nobody has touched in decades. You sell the house in its present condition and keep your weekends. What you still owe is the paperwork: tax payoffs, the deed and any permits the buyer's title agent asks about. Sorting those out early is what lets a closing happen on the date you circled on the calendar, and it spares everyone a scramble the week before.

• The most recent city and county tax bills, along with payoff figures from both offices.
  • Your deed, which shows the district, map and parcel numbers.
  • Permit records for recent remodels.
  • The rental permit and safety affidavit, if guests ever stayed there.
  • Lease terms and end dates, if someone rents the house now.

With this folder ready, a buyer can quote a firm figure fast and the title company can schedule the signing.

faqs.q: Do I pay Maryville and Blount County tax separately?
faqs.a: Yes, two separate bills arrive, each calculated at its own rate. Get a payoff from both offices ahead of closing.

faqs.q: What is the Blount County property tax calendar?
faqs.a: Statements mail in early to mid-September, and you can pay through February without penalty. March 1 is the delinquency date, and then 1.5% accrues monthly.

faqs.q: Is there a discount for paying early in Blount County?
faqs.a: Yes. Pay through October for 2% off, or in November for 1% off.

faqs.q: How much does recording a deed cost in Blount County?
faqs.a: Expect $12 for the first two pages, $5 per additional page and a $1 clerk fee. Tennessee's transfer tax adds 37 cents per $100.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Maryville permit?
faqs.a: Maryville Codes Enforcement, 865-273-3500, 416 West Broadway. Ask about permits on any past work before the house goes on the market.
